reason: The cited evidence does not involve the HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy or similar refractory high-entropy alloys; it describes different alloy systems (e.g., fcc/D019 duplex, CoCrNi-based, eutectic alloys, Ti) and processing conditions (e.g., 96% cold reduction, 750°C annealing, rapid annealing) that are not directly transferable. No evidence supports the key premises that the proposed deformation and annealing will produce a bimodal structure in this alloy or that such a structure will yield the claimed ductility-strength balance.
premises: Heavy cold deformation (~60% reduction) of HfZrTiTa0.53 can generate high dislocation densities and stored energy to drive partial recrystallization.
Low-temperature annealing (~650°C) of the cold-deformed alloy can induce a bimodal grain structure (ultrafine + larger recrystallized grains).
A bimodal grain structure promotes uniform dislocation motion and deformation twinning, delaying necking and enhancing tensile ductility.
The bimodal structure can enhance ductility without significantly compromising yield strength, compressive strength, or impact-triggered energy release.
The proposed processing is applicable to the specific HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy and will produce the predicted mechanical improvements.
